market_brief: The Nvidia shock has moved to Asia's chip names. On Monday the Taiex fell as much as 6%, Kospi more than 3% and the Nikkei about 2% (Taiwan -3.4%, KOSPI -2.5% and Nikkei -1.6% in this morning's snapshot), led by TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung and Tokyo Electron, a week after the SOX closed Friday down 3.4%. Weak data added to the pressure: Japan's Q3 GDP contracted and China's October output, retail sales and investment all missed. US futures are slightly lower ahead of Nvidia's results Tuesday, Fed minutes Wednesday and Anthropic's IPO pricing. Reports say the book is about 6x covered and banks are weighing a price above the range. Rates stay the main headwind: the US 10Y is at about 5.15% (+30bp on the week) and Fed Chair Warsh speaks today. Brent (about $95) fell for a third day on an IEA surplus forecast, even after a new Iranian strike on Bahrain. Gold (about $3,876) and BTC (about $65k, -13% w/w) are still down for the week. India is the outlier, with Nifty up about 0.4% midday on FII buying.
ai_brief: Commerce and agents led the weekend AI news: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets agents complete purchases, xAI quietly began rolling out Grok 4.8, and DeepSeek exposed its app tools through its API. Agent-infrastructure deals continued, with LangChain raising $300M at a $3B valuation and CrowdStrike reportedly paying $495M for two agent-security startups. Attention this week is on Anthropic's IPO and on Nvidia's results under an interim CEO.

items.headline: Asian chip stocks slump as Nvidia fallout spreads: Taiex down ~6%, Kospi -3.6%, Nikkei -2.4%
items.summary: On Monday, per AP, TSMC fell 5.7%, SK Hynix 7.9%, Samsung 4.5%, and Kioxia and Tokyo Electron 7-8%. Hong Kong was the exception, edging up about 0.5%. Weak Japan and China data compounded worries about AI hardware demand.

items.headline: Update: Jensen Huang reportedly discussing a return as Nvidia CEO; board also approached Arm's Rene Haas
items.summary: New since Huang's resignation: the FT reports he has discussed coming back, Elon Musk publicly backed a reinstatement petition, and investors Altimeter and Atreides urged the board to keep the option open. NVDA fell more than 12% last week to $162.85 and dropped below $4T in market value.

items.headline: Huang comeback odds: Munster says 51%, Kalshi traders say about 9%
items.summary: Deepwater's Gene Munster lifted his estimate of Huang returning to 51% from 10% on Friday. On Kalshi, prediction-market pricing was far lower at around 9%. The gap is a live debate on fintwit going into Tuesday's earnings.

items.headline: Wave of Nvidia downgrades: at least 10 analysts move to Hold, and one SA analyst goes to Sell
items.summary: Downgrades piled up after the leadership change. One Seeking Alpha analyst moved NVDA to Sell, citing the CEO exit, data-center moratoriums and hyperscaler cash burn. Tesla also got a Sell call on valuation.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic IPO book reportedly ~6x covered; underwriters weigh pricing above $70-78
items.summary: Per Reuters, orders reached about six times the shares on offer, up from roughly 2x on day one. The FT says Goldman and Morgan Stanley are weighing a price above the range. The sell side models about $52-53B of 2026 revenue, while some buy-side investors doubt Claude can keep its premium pricing. Pricing is Nov 18 and trading starts Nov 19.

items.headline: Japan Q3 GDP contracts 0.1% annualised vs +0.3% expected, ending three quarters of growth
items.summary: Weak exports and softer consumption drove the miss. It complicates the BoJ's December hike debate, with USD/JPY near 160. BoJ board member Takata also spoke on Monday.

items.headline: China's October data miss across the board: retail sales +0.4% y/y, output +4.8%, FAI -8.1% YTD
items.summary: Retail sales (vs 0.8% expected) and industrial output (vs 5.3%) both slowed from September. Fixed-asset investment fell more than forecast, though urban unemployment eased to 5.1%. The Shanghai Composite fell about 1%.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh speaks today at the SF Fed, with a December hike being debated
items.summary: Warsh gives opening remarks at a productivity conference at 12:00 ET. Last week Governor Waller said a 50bp move should be considered if core CPI keeps running near 0.3%. Goldman expects 25bp in December.

items.headline: US futures edge lower; Nasdaq futures down ~0.5% ahead of a heavy AI week
items.summary: Overnight, S&P futures were about -0.2% and Nasdaq futures about -0.6%, after Friday's split close (Dow +0.1%, Nasdaq -0.9%). The 30-year yield is near 5.47%.

items.headline: Oil slips for a third session on IEA surplus forecast despite an Iranian strike on a US base in Bahrain
items.summary: The IEA sees a Q4 surplus of roughly 1.7-2 mb/d, and observed inventories rose in October for the first time since June. Over the weekend Iran hit a US helicopter base in Bahrain and mines reportedly struck several vessels, but Brent stayed near $95.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty rise despite Asia's sell-off; mid- and small-caps lag
items.summary: By midday the Sensex was up about 0.45% near 81,960 and the Nifty about 0.35% near 25,230, helped by FII buying and softer crude. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 both fell.

items.headline: Tata Motors PV falls ~9% after a Q2 FY27 net loss of ₹5,451 crore
items.summary: The passenger-vehicle business swung to a large quarterly loss, and the stock slid on Monday.

items.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields sets IPO band at ₹129-136, valuing the Coal India unit at about $9.5B
items.summary: This is another large PSU listing in India's busy primary market.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley puts 50% odds on Sensex reaching 95,000 by December 2027
items.summary: The broker's base case implies about 16% upside from current levels.

items.headline: Week ahead: Warsh (Mon); US retail sales and Nvidia (Tue); Fed minutes and Anthropic pricing (Wed); ANT debut and Walmart (Thu)
items.summary: Also on the calendar: the PBoC LPR on Nov 23 and the Bank of Korea on Nov 26. Huang's possible return is an extra wildcard for Nvidia's call.

items.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so agents can shop and check out
items.summary: Agents can complete purchases with tokenized Amex, Mastercard and Visa cards. It is available to US Pro users aged 18+.

items.headline: xAI soft-launches Grok 4.8 without a model card or API
items.summary: Grok 4.8 is rolling out quietly to Grok users. No benchmarks, model card or API access have been published yet.

items.headline: DeepSeek opens its app tools to the API: web search, file input, OCR, speech
items.summary: A Nov 13 changelog lets developers call DeepSeek's built-in tools directly. No new model weights came with it.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly folds its standalone robotics team into research
items.summary: The robotics group was disbanded and its work moved into the research and applied organizations, per reports on Nov 13.

items.headline: LangChain raises $300M at a $3B valuation; CrowdStrike reportedly buys two agent-security startups for $495M
items.summary: CapitalG led LangChain's Series C. Separately, CrowdStrike is reported to have bought two AI-agent security firms, and Nebuly raised $21M to measure agent ROI.

items.headline: Bland AI previews Tofu-1, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model
items.summary: Tofu-1 processes audio directly rather than through transcripts. It is gated to regulated enterprises for now, with general availability slated for January.

items.headline: AMD's Zen 6 EPYC server CPUs reach GA on TSMC 2nm; Google uses EPYC hosts in TPU 8tx systems
items.summary: The flagship EPYC 9996 is reportedly priced near $14.9k per socket. Google picked AMD over its own Axion chip for confidential TPU host systems.

items.headline: EU adopts implementing rules for AI Act regulatory sandboxes
items.summary: Implementing Regulation 2026/2487, published Nov 11, sets how national AI sandboxes work. Member states must have them running by Aug 2, 2027.

items.headline: Malaysia proposes a law to track data-centre power use and curb AI GPU smuggling
items.summary: Operators would also pay for capacity they reserve but leave unused, part of tighter oversight of the country's data-centre boom.

items.headline: Stanford open-sources Memorilla, which compresses documents into 16 tokens for frozen LLMs
items.summary: Memorilla is a 194M-parameter memory module tested on a frozen Qwen3-8B. Cloudflare also put EmbeddingGemma 2 on Workers AI at very low per-token prices.

items.headline: Oura to acquire clinical-AI startup Counsel Health for $625M in cash
items.summary: The deal brings Counsel's clinical AI agents into Oura's health-wearable platform.
